questions.q: Why shouldn't most tests for AIClient call the real API?
options: The real API doesn't return JSON
Testing is unnecessary for API clients
The real API has no error responses
Real calls cost money, take real network time, and aren't deterministic enough to reliably trigger specific conditions like a 429
questions.explain: You can't reliably make a live API fail on command, and real calls cost money and time — tests should target your code's logic, not the live service.

It permanently changes the AIClient class definition
It replaces session.post with a stand-in that returns the fake response instead of making a real call
It deletes the session object
questions.explain: unittest.mock's patch.object swaps out session.post for a mock during the test, so no real network call happens.

questions.q: What does side_effect=[rate_limited, success] do on a mock?
options: It makes the mock raise an exception on every call
It returns rate_limited on the first call and success on the second, letting you simulate a retry-then-recover scenario
It ignores both arguments
It runs both responses simultaneously
questions.explain: side_effect as a list makes consecutive calls return each value in order — exactly what's needed to simulate a 429 followed by a successful retry.

questions.q: Why does the retry-loop test also patch time.sleep?
options: To make the retry loop skip retrying entirely
It's unnecessary and has no effect on the test
So the test doesn't actually pause for real seconds during the backoff wait
To simulate a slower network connection
questions.explain: Without patching time.sleep, the test would actually wait out the real backoff delays, making it slow for no benefit.

questions.q: What role do integration tests play in a healthy test suite for this client?
options: They replace unit tests entirely
They run automatically on every single commit, just like unit tests
A small, deliberate number of them call the real API — useful, but not run as freely as fast mocked unit tests
They are never useful for an API client
questions.explain: Integration tests validate real end-to-end behavior but cost money and take real time, so they're kept few and run deliberately rather than on every commit.
